html:
The Me'phaa, called Tlapanecs in Spanish, are an Indigenous people of the Montaña region of Guerrero in southern Mexico. Their language belongs to the Oto-Manguean family, like Mixtec and Zapotec.

Before 1492 their main centre was Tlapa, the seat of a small kingdom that the Aztec Triple Alliance conquered in the late 1400s and made into a tribute province. The Codex Azoyú, painted in the region, records its rulers in that era. After the Spanish conquest the Montaña remained poor and remote. Today over 100,000 people speak Me'phaa. Their neighbours include the Nahua of Guerrero and the Amuzgo.
